 179th Defense Projects Promotion Committee
Fixing Basic Strategy for Nuclear Submarine Project Promotion to Invest 870 Billion by 2031 사진 확대 Scene of the "S-92" helicopter flight of Lockheed Martin, U.S.A. [Lockheed Martin] The military has finally selected Lockheed Martin's "S-92A+" as a presidential helicopter model to be operated from 2031.
 The Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) held the 179th Defense Promotion Committee (cold) at the Ministry of National Defense building in Yongsan, Seoul, presided over by Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul on the 6th, and deliberated and decided on a decision on the "command helicopter-II" project model. The total project cost is about 873 billion won, and the newly introduced dedicated helicopter will be boarded by the next president, not the president of Lee Jae Myung.
 Earlier in April last year, the military decided to introduce four new command helicopters from overseas through the 168th cold weather and has been searching for a suitable model.
 At the time, the military said it would secure a new model with improved survival and command and control capabilities than the US Sikorsky's "VH-92," which was introduced in 2007. Since then, the company has reportedly been reviewing four candidate models, including △ Airbus H225M (France), △ Leonardo AW-101 (Italy), △ Bell 525 (US) △ Lockheed Martin S-92A+ (US).
 However, during the review process, other models met the conditions in terms of price and performance, so Lockheed Martin's "S-92A+" was reported to have participated in the bidding.
 An official from the DAPA explained, "The export of aircraft modification and maintenance technology and parts for domestic small and medium-sized enterprises secured through this project is expected to contribute to the development of the domestic defense industry and strengthening export competitiveness in the future."
 Nuclear Submarine Exempts Feasibility Study...Accelerate next year's launch 사진 확대 President Lee Jae Myung listens to then Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek's basic plan to develop nuclear-powered submarines at the 1st Future Defense Strategy Committee held in Jinhae-gu, Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province in May. [Yonhap News] The military also confirmed the basic strategy for promoting the project of Jang Bogo N, a Korean nuclear-powered submarine project, in the cold. In other words, the government has established a "master plan" for the construction of nuclear submarines and has set a timetable for future design and construction schedules to begin the project in earnest.
 The main goal of this project is to receive nuclear fuel through cooperation between the U.S. and South Korea, design and build nuclear submarines with Korea's own technology, and electrify the "No. 1 ship" by the late 2030s. After that, we also plan to secure follow-up boxes sequentially. The government is reportedly considering building about 8,000 tons of Korean nuclear submarines.
 The government has prepared a special nuclear submarine law to promote Jang Bo-go N, and plans to make pan-governmental efforts by forming a "nuclear-promoted submarine strategy committee" headed by the prime minister.
 On this day, the government also announced that it had been exempted from a feasibility study to speed up the "Jang Bo-go N" project. The project is expected to accelerate as business feasibility studies, which usually take one to two years, are exempted.
 Large weapons systems development projects such as nuclear submarines are subject to business feasibility studies under the Defense Acquisition Program Administration Act, but exceptional exemptions are possible for projects that require high security such as Jang Bo-go N. Earlier, the F-35A performance improvement project, the South Korean military's flagship fifth-generation stealth fighter, was exempted from the feasibility study.
 The government decided to push for the development and construction of nuclear submarine hulls through "competitive bidding" among domestic shipbuilders, and the state will directly secure and provide small nuclear reactors and major armed equipment.
